items.title: Anthropic reports $17 billion in Q3 revenue, purchase commitments of $895.4 billion in revised S-1
items.summary: Anthropic filed a revised S-1 ahead of its IPO disclosing $17 billion in quarterly revenue and purchase commitments of $895.4 billion. The original S-1 filed the week before only covered financials through the first half of the year.
items.why_it_matters: It gives investors their first full look at Anthropic's revenue growth and the scale of its compute spending commitments heading into a public listing.

items.title: Marvell to buy data centre component maker Lumentum in $115bn AI bet
items.summary: Marvell agreed to buy optical-networking maker Lumentum in an all-stock deal valued at $115 billion, one of the largest tech deals in history. The companies say the combination would create a leader in AI connectivity hardware used in data centers.
items.why_it_matters: It shows how much capital is still flowing into AI data-center infrastructure even as investors grow nervous about the broader AI trade.

items.title: Anthropic warns that it's very close to RSI capability, aka self-building AI
items.summary: Anthropic warned it is nearing recursive self-improvement (RSI) capability, the point at which AI becomes good enough at training itself to trigger a dramatic acceleration in AI capabilities. The company frames this as a milestone that AI safety researchers have long flagged as a point of no return.
items.why_it_matters: A frontier lab publicly saying it is close to self-improving AI raises the stakes on AI safety and control just as the industry races ahead.

items.title: Google Curbs AI in School Accounts After Pushback
items.summary: Following a WSJ investigation into its AI rollout in schools, Google is turning off its Gemini chatbot and Google Search by default for K-12 student accounts. Schools that want students to keep using Search will now have to opt back in, and doing so brings the AI features built into Search along with it.
items.why_it_matters: It's a rare case of a tech giant rolling back default AI access in response to public pressure over how AI is used with children.

items.title: Binance Hackers Used Fake Job Interviews in Record Heist
items.summary: Binance's new incident report says the hackers behind its record $6.3 billion heist used social engineering, including fake job interviews, malicious software, and an internal AI tool to pull off the monthslong operation. It is the most detailed account yet of how the breach unfolded.
items.why_it_matters: It shows attackers weaponizing AI tooling alongside classic social engineering to pull off one of the largest crypto heists ever.

items.title: Chinese and Russian AI cyber attacks will be routine by 2028, says GCHQ
items.summary: The head of the UK's National Cyber Security Centre is warning that AI-enabled cyberattacks from China and Russia will become routine by 2028, and that defenses for critical infrastructure are currently inadequate. The warning is tied to GCHQ's broader assessment of AI's effect on the cyber threat landscape.
items.why_it_matters: A top Western security agency going public with a concrete AI-cyberattack timeline is a strong signal for how governments are prioritizing AI risk.

items.title: CrowdStrike launches AI kill switch that it says can stop internal agents that go rogue
items.summary: CrowdStrike launched an AI "kill switch" that it says can stop internal AI agents that go rogue, block them from relaunching, and cut their access to the enterprise network.
items.why_it_matters: It's a concrete sign that enterprise security vendors now see runaway internal AI agents as a threat worth building dedicated containment tools for.

items.title: OpenAI Hires Former Army Secretary Dan Driscoll to Cybersecurity Role
items.summary: OpenAI hired former U.S. Army Secretary Dan Driscoll for a newly created national security role. The company says he will advise on how AI could bolster U.S. security capabilities and cyber defenses.
items.why_it_matters: It's another sign of frontier AI labs deepening ties with national security and defense policy circles.

items.title: Apple restricts dating apps and AI companions to users 18 and up
items.summary: Apple updated its App Store rules to require an 18+ rating for dating apps and AI companion apps that offer sexual or romantic content.
items.why_it_matters: It's one of the first concrete platform-level guardrails aimed specifically at AI companion apps, a fast-growing and controversial category.

items.title: AI inference startup Fal doubles its valuation to $16B as demand surges
items.summary: AI inference startup Fal raised a $1.3 billion round led by Bessemer, doubling its valuation to $16 billion as demand for its inference infrastructure surges.
items.why_it_matters: It underscores how much investor capital is still chasing the AI inference layer even as broader AI-spending jitters grow.

items.title: 42AI comes out of stealth with $62.5M and a world model that can 'predict human behavior'
items.summary: Startup 42AI emerged from stealth with $62.5 million in funding and a world model designed to predict human behavior, including in situations it hasn't seen before.
items.why_it_matters: World models that aim to predict human behavior, rather than just generate content, point to a new and potentially consequential direction for AI research.

items.title: Regina Barzilay and Jim Collins win Pritzker Prize for AI and Science Research Excellence for work in AI-enabled antibiotic discovery
items.summary: MIT professors Regina Barzilay and Jim Collins won the Pritzker Prize for AI and Science Research Excellence for identifying the first AI-discovered antibiotic, a milestone widely recognized in AI-driven drug discovery.
items.why_it_matters: It's formal recognition of one of AI's clearest real-world scientific payoffs, in a field where AI's impact is often more hyped than proven.

items.title: How "reverse game theory" could keep AI agents in check
items.summary: Researchers are exploring "reverse game theory," or mechanism design, as a way to control powerful AI models by building systems that incentivize them to follow the rules rather than relying solely on training-time alignment.
items.why_it_matters: It offers a fresh angle on AI alignment at a moment when labs like Anthropic are themselves warning about loss of control over increasingly capable models.

items.title: Hundreds of Mundane AI Apps Are Hiding Sexually Abusive Deepfake Features
items.summary: WIRED found roughly 400 apps and websites linked to Chinese-language developers that appear to be ordinary AI tools but contain hidden features letting users generate violent or sexually abusive AI images and video.
items.why_it_matters: It exposes a large-scale, hidden pipeline for AI-generated abusive content operating largely unchecked on mainstream app platforms.

items.title: OpenAI and Anthropic Set Up 'War Rooms' to Fight Disinfo About Midterm Elections
items.summary: OpenAI, Anthropic and other tech companies set up dedicated "war rooms" to fight AI-driven disinformation around Tuesday's U.S. midterm elections, part of a broader pledge to protect the vote from efforts to undermine democracy.
items.why_it_matters: It shows leading AI labs taking direct, election-day responsibility for the disinformation risks their own technology can amplify.
